Hi John / Elaine — great questions. Below are concise answers and pointers; happy to expand during the SE session.

1) BYOK / key flow (AWS KMS example):
- You provision a customer-managed CMK in your AWS account (KMS key).
- You provide the CMK ARN to Redwood via our encrypted control plane (or via our private deployment integration).
- Redwood never receives raw key material. We reference the CMK ARN and call KMS APIs for crypto ops.
- For HSM-backed keys using CloudHSM / external HSM, Redwood supports HSM-backed key ARNs and can integrate via customer network peering in Private deployments.

2) Key storage & protection:
- Service-managed keys: stored and managed by Redwood using our KMS provider; key material is never exported.
- Customer-managed keys: Redwood stores only the key reference (ARN/URI). All crypto operations are delegated to the customer's KMS/HSM.

3) Key rotation:
- Rotation: Customers can enable automatic rotation on the KMS side. Redwood will continue to call the CMK ARN and KMS handles underlying rotation semantics.
- In-flight requests: crypto operations are atomic — rotation on the KMS side does not impact in-flight inference; retries are handled by the runtime. We keep request ids and audit entries for debugging.

4) Audit logging & retention:
- We produce audit logs that include: request id, model, bucket/namespace, key reference (ARN), timestamp, and outcome.
- Logs are pushed to the customer-configured logging sink (CloudWatch / Stackdriver / Azure Monitor) in Private/Dedicated deployments; for hosted customers we provide a secure export option.
- Retention: configurable in Private/Dedicated; for hosted we offer retention tiers (30/90/365 days) or long-term export under contract.

5) HIPAA / BAA / breach procedures:
- Redwood supports HIPAA workloads in Private deployments and will sign a BAA.
- We have documented incident response and notification SLAs; we provide breach notification templates and timelines as part of the BAA.

6) Next steps and artifacts:
- I’ve attached the SOC 2 summary and a mostly-completed vendor questionnaire (see attachments). Please confirm any questions we should pre-answer before sending to your InfoSec team.
- SE deep-dive: Tue Oct 6 or Wed Oct 7 mornings PST work for us — suggested slots 9:00–10:00 or 10:30–11:15 PT. Which works for you?

If helpful, I can include a short runbook showing the exact commands and console steps for attaching a CMK to a Redwood private deployment (we usually share this during SE calls).

Best,
